text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Ruling coalition party leaders met on Monday to discuss much-needed reforms of the country's welfare system as presented in a document by centre-left government. Prime minister Romano Prodi, on a visit to the U.S., said the majority coalition was "very strong" (all).
* Hard left Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti repeated his party's stand, strongly opposed to pension spending cuts in plans for reforming the country's welfare state (all).
* Preliminary figures from eleven sample cities showed Italian consumer price inflation rose 0.1 percent month-on-month and 1.4 percent year-on-year in June against 1.6 percent in May (all).

* State industrial holding IRI said it had named Gian Maria Gros Pietro, the new chairman of the group, as managing director. Pietro Gnudi, another member of the board, was given the task of coordinating contractual and procedural aspects relating to the privatisation of IRI's subsidiaries (all).

* Gabriele Galateri, managing director of the Agnelli family industrial holding company IFIL, said the group's 1997 results will be better than in 1996. Umberto Agnelli said that Fiat's syndicate of major shareholders will have to decide who succeeds Cesare Romiti as chairman of the industrial group. Umberto Agnelli also said the entry of Agnelli family holding companies IFI and IFIL into the share capital of San Paolo bank was not meant to create a rival to merchant bank Mediobanca (all).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
